Subject: Post-demo: Performance SLO checklist & next steps (FinTechCo)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great demo today — thanks for walking us through the two main flows. As promised, attached is a first-pass SLO checklist tailored to the endpoints we discussed and a short set of next-step MAP items so we can scope a quick POC. Please review and confirm the numbers below or flag changes.

High-level SLO targets (initial proposal):
- Real-time chat/assisted-writing endpoints: p95 latency <= 200 ms (token-streaming enabled)
- High-throughput batch embedding/analysis: sustained throughput target ~500 qps (aggregate)
- Peak concurrency (concurrent sessions): 50 (with ability to burst to 120 for short campaigns)
- Streaming requirements: token-level streaming with partial responses (client must support SSE/websocket)
- Availability/SLAs: 99.9% target for dedicated deployments

Attachments: 20270528_fintechco_slo_checklist.xlsx, redwood_post_demo_notes.pdf

Next steps (proposed MAP):
1) Confirm final SLO targets and burst behavior (this thread)
2) Redwood to propose two MAP options (Dedicated reserved pool vs Hosted + burst autoscale) with estimated cost/latency tradeoffs (by end of week)
3) Run a 2-day POC perf test (we project start window: week of Jun 7)
4) Decision criteria sign-off: latency target, cost cap, and SLA requirements

Can you confirm whether streaming must be token-level for all endpoints (vs only for the chat endpoint)? Also: do you have an internal traffic matrix for expected daily/peak QPS? That'll help us size the POC.

Thanks — I copied Vivek and Aditya from our solutions team so they can propose the MAP and perf plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLO checklist & next steps (FinTechCo)

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Streaming: token-level streaming is required for the chat/assist endpoint (low-latency UI). For the batch endpoints we don't need token streaming — chunked responses are OK.

2) Latency targets: p95 <= 200ms is ideal for the chat experience, but we have a secondary tier of endpoints (reporting embeddings / background tasks) where p95 <= 300ms is acceptable. If you must pick a single conservative number for sizing the POC, 250ms would be acceptable across both classes for now.

3) Throughput / concurrency: Our normal baseline is ~300 qps, but we expect campaign peaks that push sustained bursts to ~900 qps for ~5–10 minutes; peak concurrent sessions could reach ~120 during those bursts.

4) We have an internal traffic matrix — attaching it here so you can use real numbers for sizing.

Attachment: fintechco_traffic_matrix_may2027.csv

A couple of asks: what will tail-p99 latency look like under burst vs steady-state? And can you outline how Redwood handles KV cache warming for short bursts (we're concerned about cold-start tails).

Alex
VP Product — FinTechCo
alex.chen@fintechco.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLO checklist & next steps (FinTechCo)

Marissa / Alex — quick note from the solutions/infra side.

Thanks for the traffic matrix Alex — very helpful. Two things from Redwood's side and a proposed MAP outline: 

Tail latency & bursts:
- p99 tail under short bursts is usually ~2–3x p95 for hosted endpoints unless caching and pre-warming are configured. For Dedicated pools we can hold steady p95 targets much more tightly.
- For campaign-style 5–10 minute bursts to 900 qps, we recommend either pre-warming a reserved burst pool or using a hybrid dedicated+autoscale approach with conservative warm-up parallelism.
- KV cache warmup: we can seed KV cache by replaying a small sample of representative prefixes (you can share a 1–2% sample of traffic) to reduce cold-start tails.

Proposed MAP options (high level):
1) Dedicated Reserved Pool (Option A) — consistent p95 <=200ms for chat, predictable p99 bounds, higher baseline cost but best reliability for campaigns.
2) Hosted + Dedicated Burst (Option B) — lower baseline cost; use hosted endpoints for steady-state and a pre-warmed dedicated burst pool for campaigns. Expect p95 ~220–300ms depending on burst size and cache warm state.

Next steps I recommend we include in the MAP doc:
- Perf test spec (workload, traffic matrix, scripts)
- POC dates (target start Jun 7; 48-hour perf run)
- Acceptance criteria (p95 targets per endpoint class, p99 tail threshold, error rate <0.5%)

I'll draft estimated cost/latency tradeoffs for both options and send a MAP doc by EOD.

-Vivek
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLO checklist & next steps (FinTechCo)

Alex / Priya — thanks, this is perfect. I updated the attached MAP with Vivek's notes and included a decision-criteria checklist below — please review and sign off so we can lock the POC dates.

Decision criteria (please confirm):
- Chat endpoints: target p95 <= 220 ms (FinTechCo accepts 250ms for secondary endpoints)
- P99 tail: must be < 2.5x p95 for steady-state; acceptable up to 3x during short bursts
- Peak sustained throughput for POC: test up to 900 qps for 10-minute windows
- Concurrency: validate up to 120 concurrent sessions during burst tests
- Streaming: token-level streaming required for chat endpoint; chunked streaming OK for batch/embeddings
- Acceptance: POC passes if p95 targets met for >95% of test windows and error rate <0.5%

Proposed MAP next steps (with dates):
- May 31: Redwood finalizes MAP doc and perf spec (attached MAP_fintechco_v1.docx)
- Jun 7: Start 48-hour POC perf run (we'll coordinate test window with your infra)
- Jun 11: Post-POC recap and decision meeting

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/FIN-2027-0042

Can you confirm the criteria above and confirm we should plan for Jun 7 start? If yes, we'll send the perf scripts and a short onboarding checklist for your infra team.

Thanks —
Marissa
